subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ben Jones <ben.jones@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps - token unit economics and target $/1M

Hi Ben / Sofia,

Thanks again for the call today, great to learn more about the recommendation engine workload and the monthly inference profile. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Profile you shared: ~120M prompt tokens and ~380M completion tokens per month (peak windows mid-month).
- Primary goal: reduce unit cost while keeping 95th p90 latency SLOs for live recommendations.
- Current host: mix of OpenAI + self-hosted smaller models; procurement is targeting a blended target around $400-$800 per 1M tokens (team-level target is $600/1M).

What we can do next:
1) I'll ship a short benchmarking packet comparing Redwood unit economics vs OpenAI/Anthropic for similar models (costs expressed as $/1M tokens, with notes on latency and quality tradeoffs).
2) If the numbers look promising, we can schedule a 30-min follow-up with your engineering lead to discuss a small POC (1-2 week integration + 100k-1M token test).
3) Please confirm any contractual constraints (SLA, data residency) and target procurement timeline.

I attached a benchmarking workbook and our Redwood pricing sheet - highlights in the first tab.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: token_benchmark_v2.xlsx (workbook), redwood_pricing_sheet.pdf

From: Ben Jones <ben.jones@acme.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps - token unit economics and target $/1M

Thanks Vanessa, great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The volumes I quoted are our expected production average; we have bursty days up to ~1B tokens when marketing campaigns run.
- Procurement target: the procurement committee is asking for a clear cost comparison expressed as $/1M tokens. Their initial target is ~ $500/1M (blended), but they may accept up to $750 if latency and quality are demonstrably better.
- We care about billed token definitions (prompt vs completion), need to see like-for-like. Also any hidden costs (logs, evals, network egress) should be surfaced.

Happy to run a POC - engineering can allocate a small integration window Sep 7-14. If you can get the benchmark sheet over by Friday, I'll circulate to procurement.

Ben Jones
Head of Product - Personalization
Acme AI
ben.jones@acme.ai | (650) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmarks (internal) - suggested target pricing vs hosts

Vanessa, pulling together a short note for procurement. See quick bullets below (will include tab-level numbers in the workbook):

- Redwood (recommended config: quantized LLM + batching + prefix cache): ~$220-$320 per 1M tokens (blended prompt+completion) depending on batching and persistent KV cache hit rate (60-80%).
- OpenAI (gpt-4 style / mix): ballpark $700-$1,000 per 1M tokens for similar quality on completion-heavy workloads (higher for function-calls/structured outputs).
- Anthropic: ~$650-$950 per 1M tokens depending on model and context window.
- Other open-model hosts (managed inference): $300-$500 per 1M tokens for 8-bit quantized variants, but often with tradeoffs on latency and engineering support.

Notes:
- These figures are delivered as blended $/1M (prompt + completion) to match Acme's ask. We've conservatively included network egress and logging in the Redwood estimate.
- For Acme's volume profile, our model suggests a 35-55% cost savings vs OpenAI/Anthropic at equivalent quality levels - aligns with their procurement target of ~$500/1M.
- Recommend we call out optional Dedicated pricing (committed capacity) for further unit-cost improvement; show a committed vs on-demand comparison in the deck.

I'll update the workbook with the specific lines that map to Acme's token split next. Recommend Vanessa put the procurement target ($500/1M) in the POC SOW so we can show realized numbers during the test.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer 
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ben Jones <ben.jones@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps - token unit economics and target $/1M

Ben,

Thanks - attaching the workbook with the Acme-specific tab filled out (token split, projected monthly volume, and conservative/expected/optimistic $/1M lines). Highlights: 

- Redwood on-demand estimate (conservative): $295 / 1M tokens (includes logging + standard egress assumptions).
- Dedicated/committed estimate (12-month commit, target volume): $165 / 1M tokens (requires minimum monthly commit; models and quantization profile included).
- OpenAI blended estimate (public pricing comparable models): $720 / 1M tokens (includes prompt+completion).
- Anthropic blended estimate: $680 / 1M tokens.

Action items:
- Ben: confirm procurement target ($500/1M) and whether a 12-month commit is possible for the Dedicated case.
- Acme Eng: confirm integration window Sep 7-14 for POC. We'll provide a POC SOW with a target throughput and success criteria (cost per 1M observed + latency SLOs).
- Marissa/Rachel: prepare a short one-pager showing committed vs on-demand economics and the POC acceptance criteria.

If that looks good I can schedule a 30-min slot Wed Sep 8 for a POC kickoff with engineering + procurement.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Attachments: token_benchmark_v2.xlsx, redwood_pricing_sheet.pdf
